newsitem.title: USA: Stocks hit more records, bonds weaker.
newsitem.headline: Stocks hit more records, bonds weaker.

text.p: Stocks smashed more records Friday as technology issues rallied, and the dollar surged against the German mark and other European currencies.
Bond prices weakened. Oil and gold edged lower.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 53.29 points to 6,471.76. It was the Dow's 42nd record high for 1996 and the 11th this month. The index added 123.73 for the week.
"Techs are on fire. It's a flight to earnings growth," said Philip Orlando of Value Line Asset Management.
In the broader market, advances outpaced declines, 1,497 to 956, on very heavy NYSE volume of 525.2 million shares.
The technology-studded Nasdaq composite index soared 16.28 points, or 1.3 percent, to 1,274.36, a record. The previous high of 1,270.36 was set Nov. 14. The index added 12.56 for the week.
International Business Machines Corp. added $4.375 to $158.50.
While IBM has jumped more than 70 percent from its July low, Ken Tower, a technical analyst at UST Securities, said it may rise further and that the overall market appeared healthy technically.
Despite the recent explosive rally in equities, Tower said a recent UST study showed many issues had not matched the 18 percent gains in the Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks.

Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage, noted this was a traditionally strong time of the year for the stock market, "so it would be pretty surprising to see any type of tumble here. We have lot of momentum and people are hanging onto the stocks they want. It's a supply-demand question."

One laggard group that rallied on Friday was the semiconductor equipment sector. Industry flagship Applied Materials said that even at the low point in the current cycle, it expects profit margins to remain higher than in previous market cycles, analysts said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 9/32, or $2.8125 on a $1,000 bond, raising the yield to 6.44 percent from 6.42 percent at Thursday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite direction.

In currency markets, the dollar rose against the mark and other currencies, indirectly aided by the lira's drop after Italy asked the European Union to rejoin Europe's system of semi-fixed exchange rates.
The dollar rose to 1.5073 marks late in New York from 1.4980 marks late Thursday. It rose to 111.40 Japanese yen from 111.27 yen Thursday.

The dollar also surged against the British pound, which retreated from Thursday's four-year high amid concerns that a strong pound would hurt British exports. The pound fell to $1.6795 from $1.6890 late Thurdsay.
Crude oil for January delivery fell 9 cents to $23.75 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
December gold lost 20 cents to $376.30 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange.

Overseas, London's FTSE index rose 64.9 points to 4,018.7, settling up 60.5 points for the week. In Tokyo, the key Nikkei 225 average added 72.77 points to 21,216.11, a jump of 286.38 from last Friday's close.
